title: House
description: House is the most soulful of the 6 base genres. It's also the simplest, the oldest, and the most human-sounding, which is why it stands as the world's perennial party music.

title: Acid House
description: This is the stuff that started it all--England in 1988 and all that crap. With such weird-sounding, repetitive music like this, its no wonder the public immediately associated such a vibrant music scene with rampant drug use.

title: Anthem House
description: Also called 'Stadium House' for its overuse of drum rolls (builds) and chorus fanfares (anthems) that conjure up images of hands-in-the-air antics amidst thousands of people in giant soccer stadiums and superclubs.

title: Booty House
description: Music not meant to be taken seriously--except for maybe the religious right. Combines hard house with the most offensive lyrics this side of the Parental Advisory Authority. Very habit-forming.

title: Classic House
description: Chicago House. It's antecedents include funk, soul, blues, jazz, disco, dub, and sometimes even hip hop. The result is a highly convoluted social phenomenon arising in Chicago in the mid-80s, courtesy of Frankie Knuckles.

title: Club House
description: Top40 or Eurodance music. Very poppy. Also called Handbag due to its appeal among girls who would dance in flocks around piles of their handbags on the dancefloor. Enjoyed Next Big Thing status for awhile in the mid-90s.

title: Dark House
description: With its dark, moody undertones, somewhat abrasive samples and slow, pulsing, distorted beat, this is pretty much about as evil as house music is willing to sound. Oooooooooh, scary!

title: Deep House
description: Music for the mature crowd. Very hard to find someone under 25 on the dancefloor when this is playing. Often used as wind-down music, quite simply because nothing else will do at 6 am. Good head-bobbing music.

title: Disco House
description: The music of choice in gay club culture, invariably making it the style of music that has the most fun. It's Disco. It's House. What more is there to say?

title: Disco
description: The gold chain adorning, hairy chest revealing, polyester suit wearing, John Travolta  worshipping, original floor filler. Instrumental in its influence on latter house styles.

title: Epic House
description: Basically Anthem House Lite. A more ethereal, atmospheric style of Progressive House, with romantic piano chords, swelling rhythms, and lovely female vocals. Sometimes cheesy, but not always.

title: French House
description: Also called Tekfunk or Filter House because of its heavy use of filter effects on practically everything. Has been gaining popularity the last few years, and especially since Madonna has gotten into it.

title: Funky House
description: Funky House is often used as the umbrella term for the brand of House that uses bass rhythms to move the dancefloor. Especially if that bass is funky. Accessible and popular, this music breaches Top40 radio from time to time.

title: Garage
description: The cousin of House, arising in New York at around the same time that House was being invented in Chicago. The difference between the two? Garage is deeper and more soulful, and contains more percussion.

title: Ghetto House
description: Like Ghetto Tech only with a 4/4 beat. Borrows rhythms (and probably equipment) from Tech House and lyrics from Booty House. Very fun and silly music.

title: Hard House
description: REAL Hard House. With a distorted bassdrum. And relatively little else. Good for anger management, or just hopping around pumping a fist into the air.

title: Hip House
description: House with Hip Hop influences. Likes to use lots of samples, raps, MCs, and other elements of Hip Hop culture. Another cross-bred subgenre.

title: Progressive House
description: Called Progressive because the track 'progresses' towards a climax using builds, anthems, verse-and-choruses and other cheesey elements normally reserved for pop music. Up-beat, accessible, and often gimmicky.

title: Speed Garage
description: Garage beat with somewhat goofy-sounding anthem basslines that are anything BUT funky, and horribly overused time-stretched vocals. A novelty genre of the late 90's.

title: Stupid House
description: My own term to describe the music that evolved from Nu NRG (in the Trance section) using the cheesiest elements of Progressive House, horrendously abused hoover sounds, and inane off-beat basslines. Or just anything off the Tidy Trax label.

title: Tech House
description: Simply put, TechHouse is House with the repetitive, robotic feel of Techno, hence the name. There are actually two sub genres of this: UK and Detroit. The sample here is the UK variant. Detroit Tech House just sounds a lot like oldskool Techno.

title: Tribal House
description: Bongo Drums added to House music for primal flavour. All things considered, this might very well be the oldest form of music in the history of the world. So get naked and dance around the bonfire.

title: Vocal House
description: Also called Diva House, for very good reason. Was more popular in the early 90s, now mostly played at upscale, high-class clubs. Piano chords and wailing females, this music is often interchangeable with Club House.

title: Trance
description: Trance is the most emotional genre. At one time it was very repetitive and hypnotic (hence the label 'trance'), but now it just sounds like commercial pop music more than anything else.

title: Acid Trance
description: Trippy. Fluent. Hypnotic. The stuff of real trance. Parties of this type would often last several days, aided by psychoactive drugs and a continuous stream of music.

title: Ambient Trance
description: Was a reaction to all the styles of techno that kept getting progressively harder in the early 90s. Simple techno rhythm with smooth washes and soundscapes, and lovely synths and samples on top.

title: Anthem Trance
description: Also called Stadium Trance, for obvious reasons. Glowstick waving music. Standard prog. English superclub massive music that has somehow made deities of mediocre DJs. This track should've been called Euro.

title: Booty Trance
description: Is there such a thing? Not sure, but the sample here seems to explain it perfectly. I only hope there's more of this stuff out there because I like what I've heard so far.

title: Break Trance
description: Many of yesteryear's Prog. Trance producers are now getting into this and Tech Trance, bringing in other music styles and influences to reform a sound that had, by the late 90s, become formulaic, predictable and boring (ala Anthem Trance).

title: Dark Trance
description: Dark and moody overtones. Distorted synths. Thick beat. Like Goa, but without all the busy layers and trippy samples. Not as psychedelic or spiritual either. Frightfully disturbing, if anything.

title: Death Trance
description: Also known as EBM--Electronic Body Music. One step away from Industrial. Takes ideas from Hardcore more than anything else. Relatively scary music insofar as Trance goes.

title: Dream Trance
description: Pretty much the music of one guy--Robert Miles, but immensely popular for its catchy piano riffs and dreamy soundscapes. Considered the cheesiest Trance music in existence.

title: Epic Trance
description: Lighter Progressive Trance variant. Uses pianos, lovely melodies and soft beats. Almost always contains vocals, usually female. The form of trance most likely to make Top40 play.

title: Goa Trance
description: Hippies love this stuff. Very fast, very busy, very complicated. Very spiritual, with or without mind-altering drugs. Mindfuck music, hence its alias 'Psychedelic Trance'. Imported from India, duty free--Hindu influences included.

title: Hard Acid Trance
description: Exactly what it implies. Hard. Acid. Trance. Uptempo, driving, pulsing, unrelenting beats and blistering acid lines, that instead of filling dancefloors, seek to flatten dancefloors.

title: Hard Trance
description: Also known as Hardfloor. The beat is distorted into its own driving bass magnet. Very little use of melody or percussion. Often used as a 'bridge' track by Prog. Trance DJs between crescending Anthems.

title: Hi NRG
description: Actually has a storied history, emerging from Disco with Electric Boogie and Italo in the 80's. By 1990 it had become THE form of music most people associated with the word 'Techno'. Faster, more upbeat, synthetic form of Club House. Cheese.

title: Ibiza Trance
description: A natural evolution from Balearic House, the music popular in Ibiza in the mid-80s. Very soft and atmospheric, like a setting Mediterranean sunset.

title: Nu NRG
description: Erringly referred to as 'UK Hard House' for reasons unknown as it sounds neither hard nor housey. It Takes the Hard Acid Trance sound, makes the beat faster and poppier, and replaces the acid with hoovers. Lots of them.

title: Progressive Trance
description: The quintESSENTIAL genre of the British clubbing scene in the late 90s. So called because the tracks 'progress' to a crescending climax. Good trance DJs intersperse all kinds of trance genres in their sets. Bad trance DJs (and there are a lot of them) do not.

title: Symphonic Trance
description: Not a very popular or even well known genre, probably due to its application: the use of real symphonies rather than electronic or digitized ones. Classical music with a drum machine. Often used in movie soundtracks.

title: Tech Trance
description: Relatively new. Takes Progressive, does away with the melodies and synth lines, and concentrates on a myriad of beats and sounds, giving it a 'Techno' feel. Considered retro by some--simply trance returning to its anthem-less roots.

title: Tribal Trance
description: Trance with primitive, tribal feel. Emphasis on drums. Basically an upbeat repetitive version of Tribal House with less bass and funk. And likely more drugs.

title: Jungle
description: Jungle is the aggressor of the musical genres. Even its namesake speaks of raw, primitive militarism. The cleaner variant of Jungle, Drum n Bass, is very formulaic and hence trendy.

title: Atmospheric Jungle
description: Sometimes also called Ambient Jungle or Trip-jungle, this takes the smooth acid-washes and soundscapes of Ambient and sets them against a light, smooth jungle beat. Good music for driving out in the countryside.

title: Darkcore
description: Also known as Darkside. Almost in reaction to the silly, spastic sounds of Oldskool Rave Hardcore, Darkcore emerged with a deep, evil sound that would influence latter ventures into Jungle and Drum n Bass.

title: Darkstep
description: Evil stuff. Experimentation into bleak drum patterns, distorted basslines and filter effects result in a dark, moody, irrational sense of foreboding.

title: Drum n Bass
description: Exactly what it implies: a simple (usually 2-step) drum beat, and a dominating bassline, making it cleaner, smoother, more predictable and less 'primeval' than its comparatively erratic counterpart, Jungle.

title: Experimental Jungle
description: A cacophony of unique sounds, snares, rolls, and complicated drum patterns makes this one of those genres you have to acquire a taste for. Sometimes also called Intelligent Jungle simply for its sheer complexity.

title: Futurestep
description: Electro meets Drum n bass. A relatively new and promising genre, Using complex drum patterns with digitized synths, giving it that ominous, dystopian feel. The coolest thing to come out of drumnbass in recent years.

title: Hardstep
description: Drum machines slamming down the beats with authority. Heavy distortion on the bass, the percussion, and pretty much anything else. Good stomping, fist-pumping music.

title: IDM
description: It stands for Intelligent Dance Music. Jokingly called Drill n Bass or Broken Beats. Consists of a whole slew of trippy effects and complicated patterns, heavily tweaked and experimented on. Music meant to be listened to.

title: Jazzstep
description: Also called Jazzy Jungle. Drum patterns with Jazz influences, orchestrations, female (usually) vocalizations, and rhythms. Music meant for diners and coffee houses rather than clubs and raves.

title: Jump up
description: Every song is the same. EVERY GOD DAMN SONG!!! The beat is exactly the same in every track! The only thing that changes is the rolling bassline--and not by much. That makes this, by far, the most predictable music on the planet.

title: Jungle
description: A greater focus on beats, and less emphasis on bass. Complicated snare patterns and interesting percussions give this music a raw, tribal feel--hence its appropriate name, Jungle. Military motif not included.

title: Oldskool Rave Hardcore
description: Also called Breakcore, this is the music that dominated the early 90s and influenced all latter forays into Jungle and Hardcore. With spastic beats and chipmunk female vocals, its drug-fueled, high energy enthusiasm was simply referred to as: Rave.

title: Ragga Jungle
description: Also called Dancehall Jungle. Crazy snare rolls and Reggae MCs. The roots of the whole genre, by some accounts--that it may in fact have gotten its name from a ghetto in Kingston, Jamaica called 'The Concrete Jungle.'

title: Techstep
description: Two-step at its finest. Repetitive and urgent, like Techno. Very little bass involved. May be considered 'minimal drum n bass', in that respect. Often used by DJs as 'bridge' tracks in between bass-driven floor-fillers.

title: Breakbeat
description: Breakbeat is the music with the most history and the most success, which also explains why it is the music that has the most hang-ups with just about everything else.

title: 2-step Garage
description: Also called UK Garage, though it has nothing to do with actual Garage. But it does employ those foolish, dulled Speed Garage basslines, which is likely where it got its name from. It has a simplfied, 2-step beat too. This genre is quite vapid.

title: Acid Breaks
description: Pounding, thick breaks with busy soundscapes and plenty of acid to go around. Received much commercial success with entries in movie promos, sports clips and hilight reels, and spastic television advertisments.

title: Acid Jazz
description: Also called Jazzdance. The name is a misnomer, since it is neither Acid nor Jazz. Well, sort of. It is closer akin to Trip Hop, with samples, rhythms and melodies coming from more contemporary influences. Easy listening stuff.

title: Anthem Breaks
description: Stadium Breaks. Big builds, breakdowns, anthem choruses, and fanfares normally found in the House and Trance versions, only with a steady breakbeat instead. Triumphant arm-raising music.

title: Big Beat
description: Its really only the Chemical Brothers, and maybe a few other artists as well. Still, their commercial success makes this a very popular genre. Big booming Breaks, with all emphasis on the slamming beat. Distorted synths accompany.

title: Chemical Breaks
description: The West Coast sound. It refers to the amount of distortion in the synthlines. It's always digitized and skipping, giving it a very synthetic and chemical feel. Techno influences abound. Sometimes acid, but not always.

title: Dark Breaks
description: Dark, evil sounds and samples. heavy effects everywhere. The beat is displaced by sirens and glares, giving an awful sense of urgency and wrongfulness. What fun!

title: Electro
description: The perennial genre of robots and cyborgs, that gave rise in the early 80s to breakdance culture and, later on, Techno itself. Unfeeling, unemotional machine music. Zany!

title: Funky Breaks
description: Breakbeats with a grooving, funky bassline. Sometimes used as the umbrella term for all forms of breaks that have dominant basslines. Great fun all around.

title: Ghetto tech
description: Miami Bass crossed with Detroit Techno and spiced up with the most offensive pornographic lyrics of Booty House. It's the best of all worlds, making it arguably the greatest form of music ever!!!

title: Hip Hop
description: Probably the most influential music of the latter half of the 20th century. What began as simple MCing over bare-bones rhythms has become a full-fledged industry devoted to sucking money out of white middle-class youths.

title: Miami Bass
description: Music where the bass replaces the beat (bassbeat), resulting in a very deep, powerful sound. Split-off genres of this sound include Miami/Florida breaks. Gang vocals, raps, and electro influences abound. Received much commercial success.

title: Nu Electro
description: An upgraded, updated, over produced version of Electro. With bass. Not appreciated by some because it does not have the same retro feel of making the music with frustrating analog machines or the same sense of alarming despair that Electro does.

title: Nu Skool Breaks
description: A genre that can't seem to make up its mind on what to sound like. Is it just reproduced Miami Bass? Is it just Jungle slowed down? Or is it just trying too hard to sound different? Whatever it is, expect 3 or 4 genres to come out of it within a few years.

title: Progressive Breaks
description: Songs. That are sung. With lyrics, vocals, choruses, guitars and other elements of pop/rock music. Only with heavy breakbeats. Very commercial and trendy, most likely to be found on the soundtrack of the latest action movie.

title: Progressive Hop
description: Hip hop, except with stronger emphasis on the music. The Funky breakbeats are more inventive and danceable. The samples and bad-ass MCing on top are meant to enhance the beat, not replace it. More interesting than hip hop.

title: Tribal Breaks
description: Polyrhythmic blend of primal drums and nifty break beats. Sometimes uses bass, but not always. Often used by DJs as a 'bridge' track inbetween bass-heavy breakbeat anthems and crowd-pleasers.

title: Trip Hop
description: Down-tempo, deep, subdued beats. Female vocals and other elements are minimal. Easy-listening electronic music. All the major artists of this genre seem to originate from the same place--Bristol. Hmmmm.

title: Turntablism
description: The idea that a record could be scratched and back-spinned as a deliberate feature warrants much praise. With that said, from a technical standpoint, turntablists are easily the most skilled DJs on the planet. Respect.

title: Techno
description: Techno is the depressing, gritty dystopian genre. But what it lacks in soul it more than makes up in purity of sound and a mythology so romantic that it can't possibly figure out what to do with itself anymore.

title: Acid Techno
description: The acid is less warm and forgiving than in other genres. Here it's more abrasive, more unfeeling, more chemical, proving the limitless uses and moods that can be conveyed through the 303. Yummy stuff!

title: Ambient
description: Also called Chill-out music. Actually pioneered in the 70s by Brian Eno, and gained popularity in the early 90s in the chill rooms of rave parties as a means for ravers to cool down and unwind. Beat-less music. Ahhhhhhhhh....

title: Bangin' Techno
description: Called Bangin' because it focuses on a polyrhythmic, unrelenting pattern of drums, beats, and sound effects, making it one of the more enjoyable genres of Techno to listen to. A minimal subgenre of this has been spawned called Hard Minimal Shit.

title: Classic Techno
description: Techno letting its Electro-inspired roots show. Primitive machines belching out Nintendo zaps, Star Trek tweets and other futuristic computerized lazers and sounds that give the genre its namesake. Makes me wanna play Transformers.

title: Dark Ambient
description: Exactly what the name implies. Instead of lovely, smooth, swelling soundscapes as in Ambient, the music is dark and evil sounding. Makes for good Halloween music. A sub-genre, Illbient, sounds a lot like subdued Trip Hop.

title: Deep Techno
description: Minimal Techno sent through a filter. Low rhythms, heavy bass, little or no percussion at all. This genre is often used as an underlying rhythm for more distinctive and melodic Techno tracks played on top.

title: Detroit Techno
description: Very uptight and pretentious about what it considers to be deviation from the purity of its sound. Polyrhythmic and demanding. Has the feel of being urgent and distressing. If, by chance, you are on the 313 list and you disagree with what I've said here, then make a name for yourself: write your own god damn guide to electronic music and right my wrongs.

title: Dub Techno
description: Borrowing influences from Dub House, for the most part. Smooth, filtered, subdued and soulful. About as soulful as Techno music is willing to sound. Good subwoofer music.

title: Experimental Techno
description: Also known as Intellitechno. Forays into weird soundscapes, effects, patterns, digitized synths and quick cuts/edits. Not as focused on drum patterns as Experimental Jungle and IDM are, but rather on interesting sounds that are pleasant to listen to.

title: Hard Acid Techno
description: Often referred to as Filthy Acid Techno. The acid is more busy, distorted and abrasive than the Hard Acid Trance version. The  beat is colder but oftentimes faster.

title: Minimal Techno
description: It can be either just a simple beat and  a sound effect or two, or it can have  lots of busy layers that, due to their  arrangement, make the music sound  very basic. It is thus simultaneously  appreciated for its complexity and  simplicity.

title: Swedish Techno
description: European variant. Other sub genres include Belgian Techno and German Techno. Focuses on the idea of using drum patterns and rhythms as melody. After awhile, it begins to sound like it, too. Cool eh?

title: Tribal Techno
description: The most primitive-sounding of all the Tribal-related genres, because of its lack of any real percussion, melody or bass. It's just a straight polyrhythm of intersecting drums.

title: Hardcore
description: Hardcore is a musical genre with a split personality: Half of it is blistering, sadistic anger; the other half is way too silly and stupid to take its anger seriously.

title: Digital Hardcore
description: Punk-influenced Hardcore. Lots of distortion, screaming gang vocals, digitized guitar sounds and samples. Very abrasive, noisy stuff. The louder the better. The thrash metal of electronic music. Yaaay!

title: Freeform
description: Currently vying for Next Big Thing status. Takes the driving, pulsing beat of Nu NRG, the builds and breakdowns of Progressive Trance, and the speed and giddyness of Happy Hardcore--without so much cheese. Sounds promising!

title: Gabber House
description: The cheesiest cheese that you will ever cheese on. Even the names of the artists who make this stuff are cheesy. Cheesy Hoover anthems abound. Most wouldn't even call this Hardcore. Absolute pure cheese.

title: Gabber
description: The North American variety. Harder, meaner sound. Faster, thicker beat. Scary synths and angry lyrics. Music meant for releasing pent-up frustration. Also great music for a romantic evening by a roaring fire.

title: Happy Gabber
description: A logical progression from Oldskool Rave Hardcore: chipmunk vocals and silly anthems with a thundering, distorted 4/4 Hardcore beat. Quite silly, to say the least. But not necessarily cheesy.

title: Happy Hardcore
description: The biggest of the Hardcore genres because it's so poppy. Ping-pong sounding beat. Pianos. Builds. Female sing-a-long choruses. No candy raver can resist bouncing to such addictive music. Utter cheese, but somehow that's not a bad thing.

title: Metalcore
description: My own term to describe the brand of Hardcore that remixes death metal. Or maybe just death metal bands that use drum machines because their drummers can't keep up. Guitars. Long hair. Menacing vocals. Fun stuff!

title: Noize
description: Noizecore: Either its truly ground breaking, revolutionary stuff, or someone dropped a cat on the equipment. The purpose of Noize isn't that it's music, but that it's anti-music. And it's meant to be appreciated for that fact alone.

title: Rotterdam
description: European Gabber. Invariably more cheesey than the North American equivalent. The beat is slower but more distorted, and it likes to employ anthem hoovers. Rotterdam was the first style of music to use hoovers, actually.

title: Speedbass
description: What is Speedbass??? The official definition is that it apparently has NO definition. There is no specific musical characteristic that captures the Speedbass sound. The sample I have here is from the first track I got off of speedbass.com. It's as good as any.

title: Speedcore
description: Fast. Faster. Fastest. 220bpm and beyond. DO NOT try to dance to this stuff, unless your drugs permit it (which they probably don't). With so much distortion, its hard to tell what else is going on other than the beat.

title: Terrorcore
description: Also called Doomcore. Emphasis on horror and occult themes. It seeks to scare and frighten. Sounds of death, sacrifices, and all things evil and unholy. Great music for planning your next Pagan ritual or whatever.

title: Trancecore
description: Hardcore with snazzy Anthems and trancey synthlines. Not as cheesy as some of the other hoover-driven genres, but silly enough. Good music for your next hunting trip or Bar Mitzvah or whatever.
